evidence: AGENTS.md:1053-1054 -- **Library**: Use local `components/` for symbols/footprints. **Do not rely on global libraries.**
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the global libroot dependency and unconditional shutil.copy2 from build(); require each authored footprint to exist in native-19/candidate-libs and load it there. Keep any future library acquisition as an explicit separate update. Replay in an isolated output copy with the installed footprint directory unavailable or altered, then confirm the footprint-library hashes stay unchanged and the expected board/parity checks still pass.
findings.title: Replay must use the committed footprint libraries
findings.why_it_matters: Rebuilding native19 overwrites the reviewed candidate-local footprints with whichever versions are installed in the machine's KiCad application, and fails when that macOS installation path is unavailable even though the required footprints are already committed. The baseline-board hash and pad/net identity checks do not pin those replacement footprint geometries. Loading the committed candidate-libs directly preserves the reviewed R5/HOT5 geometry and satisfies the explicit local-library rule.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added build_candidate.py:63-72 unconditionally overwrites candidate-local footprint files from the installed KiCad directory before loading them, and the documented replay invokes this path with nonempty poses including R5, so a changed installed footprint replaces the reviewed geometry without a geometry hash guard, contrary to AGENTS.md:1053-1054; current local and installed R5 hashes match, so differing-library incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Source rebuild can validate an older native circuit
findings.why_it_matters: The documented reproduction sequence audits freshly compiled top-level frozen exports but regenerates the PCB and schematic from the separate native-19/frozen exports, which the sequence never updates or compares. A changed source export can therefore pass the source audit while DRC/ERC validate the previous circuit; their mutual schematic parity cannot reveal that both consumed the stale copy. The presently committed copies do match, so this is a reproduction/verification defect rather than evidence that the saved candidate is mismatched.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added reproduction-commands.json:20-37 copies and audits only top-level frozen exports, while build_candidate.py:43-45 and build_schematic.py:31-33 consume native-19/frozen without synchronization or equality checks, so a source revision that passes the audit while the native snapshot remains old reaches both builders unchanged; all three current snapshot pairs have matching SHA256 hashes, and divergent-source incidence was not measured.
